facts.value: Browser-first architectural plan and lightweight BIM editor for independent architects and small practices.
Pre-release; active technical validation and vertical-slice implementation.
New project → dimensioned residential plan → coordinated 3D → scaled vector PDF, with close/recover/reopen verification.
Semantic model/project data is authoritative; renderer objects and derived caches are disposable projections.
.arq direction is a native SQLite application database, not a renamed ZIP archive.
The .arq format/open/migration/recovery library exists, but STATUS says the end-to-end project-open pipeline is not yet reachable from the product.
The current Open project UI can read/detect/preflight selected files and honestly stops before claiming a native project is loaded.
Current plan canvas supports wall drawing, snapping, selection, pan/zoom and typed validation before commit.
Door/window/room tools/libraries are present in repository design/editor libraries but STATUS says they are not yet wired to the canvas.
Current web editor journals plan edits to IndexedDB and can replay the journal on startup.
No remote sync backend is operating in the current product.
STATUS contains contradictory statements: one says ModelCanvas is a working consumer; another says the 3D stack has zero consumers/no 3D surface.
facts.rule: Resolve against code/tests before publishing a stronger current claim.

facts.value: Bounded AI modifications are Release 3 scope; no AI-driven authoring is in the current development build.
AI cannot bypass deterministic validation, permissions or required approval; no hidden mutation.
Pricing has not been set. Current public copy says the development build is free while pre-release.
Arq does not certify professional approval, regulatory/code compliance, structural/fire/accessibility safety/compliance, cost accuracy, constructability or design correctness.
Current public support/product questions route to repository issues; security vulnerabilities route privately.
